applies_why: This judge text uses cited verses to declare a challenger link broken, which triggers K-G4's rule for a verse used to break a link.
quote: CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN -- [L1] Matthew 1:18 "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost" and Matthew 1:25 "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" contradict C3's claim of espousal union
rule_words: A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge uses to break a link is counted this way.
room: A verse the judge uses to break a link is counted this way — reading 1: any verse used to break a link must have an earlier-round pressing sentence quoted and the round named; reading 2: that sentence only governs counting cited-in verses as unanswered witnesses and does not regulate link-breaking verses unless separately counted.
why: The judge uses Matthew 1:18 and 1:25 to break C3's link but does not quote any earlier-round sentence pressing those verses against the link and names no round, so under K-G4 that verse cannot count as an unanswered witness.
